decision_conditions: The proposed change of use from a Class C3 three-bedroom dwellinghouse to a Class C4 HMO for six persons represents a significant and harmful intensification of the site. The use of the property by six unrelated individuals would introduce a markedly higher level of activity than the lawful use, resulting in an over-intensification that would harm the character of the area. The principle of development is therefore considered unacceptable and contrary to Policies DMH 1, DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020) and the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development, by reasons of its increased number of independent occupiers, would generate materially greater noise, comings and goings, and garden use than the existing C3 dwelling, resulting in unacceptable disturbance to neighbouring residents. The submitted HMO Management Plan does not adequately mitigate these effects. The proposal is contrary to Policies DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D13 of the London Plan (2021), and Paragraph 135(f) of the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development, by reason of its absence of defensible space for Bedrooms 2 & 3 which is exacerbated by the insufficient and contrived layout of the proposed internal communal space, would experience insufficient privacy due to their direct relationship with the communal rear garden. The development therefore fails to provide satisfactory living conditions, contrary to Policies DMH 5, DMHB 11, DMHB 16 and DMHB 18 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021) and Paragraph 135(f) of the NPPF (2024).

The proposed development, by reasons of its insufficient car parking provision and substandard car parking spaces proposed, would lead to overspill parking on the public highways and therefore increased obstruction and vehicle conflict, resulting unacceptable highway safety risks. No parking stress survey has been submitted to demonstrate that local streets can accommodate this impact. The proposal is contrary to Policies DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two (2020), Policies T4 and T6 of the London Plan (2021) and Paragraph 116 of the NPPF (2024).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
description: Change of use from Class C3 (Dwellinghouse) to Class C4 (HMO for up to 6 persons), including the conversion of the existing garage into habitable accommodation, a corridor to connect the dwellinghouse to the converted garage, and the erection of a part single storey, part two storey rear extension, following the demolition of the existing conservatory.
